\begingroup\small
\begin{itemize}
\item[\textbf{B1}] R. B. Sparkman, \emph{The Art of Manipulation} (1978). Contributed: the street-level tactic set (Tactics 1-14), character typologies, the financial-dealings defence, the unargue method, and the closing cost chapter.
\item[\textbf{B2}] Bookey, \emph{Art of Manipulation (condensed study summary of B1)} (2025). Contributed: a chapter-level outline of B1 used only to cross-check B1 coverage. Secondary witness: where B1 and B2 disagree, B1 wins; B2 never originates a claim.
\item[\textbf{B3}] Robert Greene, \emph{The 48 Laws of Power} (1998). Contributed: the 48-law strategic layer: reputation, attention, dependence, courtiership, timing, concealment, conflict doctrine, and the reversal device.
\item[\textbf{B4}] Robert B. Cialdini, \emph{Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion} (1984). Contributed: the laboratory mechanism layer: the automatic compliance patterns, their trigger features, and the field evidence behind reciprocation, commitment, social proof, liking, authority and scarcity.
\item[\textbf{B5}] Chris Voss (with Tahl Raz), \emph{Never Split the Difference} (2016). Contributed: the live interaction protocol: mirrors, labels, calibrated questions, the power of No, anchoring and the Ackerman plan, plus the detection doctrine (three channels, black swans).
\item[\textbf{B6}] George K. Simon Jr., \emph{In Sheep's Clothing: Understanding and Dealing with Manipulative People} (1996). Contributed: the clinical character layer: the covert-aggressive personality and its victim signature, the working tactic catalogue (guilt, shaming, the victim and servant roles, seduction, the anger display, the evasive answer), the target-side vulnerabilities, and the counter-doctrine of judging deeds, not intentions.
\item[\textbf{B7}] Philip Houston, Michael Floyd, with Susan Carnicero, \emph{Spy the Lie: How to Spot Deception the CIA Way} (2012). Contributed: the formal detection instrument: the stimulus-timed behavioural model (five-second window, cluster rule), the three-lie taxonomy with its verbal indicator catalogue, the nonverbal indicators, the counterattack tell, and the question-craft doctrine (cliff moments, entrenchment timing, the reserve rule).
\item[\textbf{B8}] Charles F. Bond, Jr. and Bella M. DePaulo, \emph{Accuracy of Deception Judgments} (2006).
\item[\textbf{B9}] Stanley Milgram, \emph{Behavioral Study of Obedience} (1963).
\end{itemize}
